title: Belief Cascades Drive Persuasion in LLM Agent Networks
abstract: arXiv:2608.25152v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly debate answers, coordinate research, simulate users, and mediate information flows, making agent-to-agent persuasion a basic but undermeasured capability. We introduce a controlled testbed for studying how goal-directed persuaders shift elicited stances in networks of LLM agents grounded in real-world ego-network topologies. Across four LLM backbones, five graphs, and 55 policy statements, we find that persuasion dynamics depend on the interaction between topology, competition, topic, and model prior. Additionally, we show that direct exposure reliably predicts next-round stance change in competing runs, and peer relays carry smaller but measurable influence, showing that agents not assigned to persuade can still transmit persuasive force. Finally, analyzing post text alone misses important movement: planned strategies are only partly realized in executed messages, action choices can diverge from mess

translated_title: 信念级联驱动LLM智能体网络中的说服效应
translated_abstract: 多智能体LLM系统日益用于辩论答案、协调研究、模拟用户和调解信息流，这使得智能体间的说服成为一种基础但未被充分衡量的能力。我们引入了一个受控测试平台，用于研究目标导向的说服者如何在基于真实世界自我网络拓扑的LLM智能体网络中改变既定立场。在四种LLM骨干、五个图和55个政策声明中，我们发现说服动态依赖于拓扑、竞争、主题和模型先验之间的交互。此外，我们表明在竞争性运行中，直接接触可靠地预测下一轮立场变化，而同伴中继传递较小但可测量的影响，显示未被指派说服任务的智能体仍能传播说服力。最后，仅分析帖子文本会遗漏重要动态：计划策略在已执行消息中仅部分实现，行动选择可能与消息内容产生分歧。
tldr: 本研究通过受控测试平台揭示，LLM智能体网络中的说服效果受拓扑、竞争、主题和模型先验交互影响，且未指派说服任务的智能体也能通过同伴中继传递说服力，仅分析文本会遗漏关键动态。
en_tdlr: This study uses a controlled testbed to show that persuasion in LLM agent networks depends on interactions among topology, competition, topic, and model priors, with non-assigned agents transmitting persuasive force via peer relays, and text-only analysis missing key dynamics.
